overview: Two categories of RNA virus genome polarity, which determine whether the viral genome can be translated directly or must first be transcribed.
genZNote: Positive-sense RNA: ready to read immediately. Negative-sense RNA: needs a translator (RdRp) before anyone can understand it.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Viruses whose genomic RNA has the same sequence/polarity as mRNA and can be translated directly by host ribosomes.
aspects.valueB: Viruses whose genomic RNA is complementary to mRNA and must first be transcribed into a positive-sense copy before translation.

aspects.label: Immediate Infectivity of Genome
aspects.valueA: The genome itself is infectious — injecting purified genomic RNA into a cell can initiate infection.
aspects.valueB: The genome alone is not infectious; it requires a virion-packaged RNA-dependent RNA polymerase to make it functional.

aspects.label: Enzyme Carried in the Virion
aspects.valueA: Generally does not need to carry RNA-dependent RNA polymerase in the virion, since host ribosomes can translate it directly.
aspects.valueB: Must carry its own RNA-dependent RNA polymerase inside the virion, since the host cannot translate negative-sense RNA.

aspects.label: Examples
aspects.valueA: Poliovirus, hepatitis C virus, SARS-CoV-2, dengue virus.
aspects.valueB: Influenza virus, rabies virus, measles virus, Ebola virus.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Genome directly translatable; equivalent to mRNA.
aspects.valueB: Genome complementary to mRNA; requires RdRp to be functional.
